data.title: Android Device Discovery & Live Mirroring
data.goalStatement: Everything needed to get a live Android screen into the window: launch-time adb/idb tool detection with per-platform toolbar status dots, the Android/iOS platform switch (Android functional in v1), the device picker with Physical and Emulator sections including inline Boot for shut-down emulators and arrow-key/Enter navigation, the primary 'Start mirroring' action over adb + scrcpy, the 2s-polling 'NO SIGNAL' empty state with inline emulator boot, and the status bar reporting tool version, resolution, fps and latency. Why: the live mirror is the annotation surface and the whole product's entry point; low latency here (NFR-1) is what makes drag-and-freeze feel responsive.
data.rawDescription: Spec F-2 delivers the complete device discovery and live mirroring pipeline for Android in v1. Built on top of the merged F-1 shell foundation (RectifyWindowShell, toolbar slots, status bar), this spec makes every toolbar and status-bar stub live. Scope: launch-time adb/idb tool detection with per-platform green/offline status dots in the toolbar; Android/iOS platform switch (Android functional in v1, iOS deferred); device picker as a centered modal panel showing detected Physical devices and Emulators with inline Boot button for shut-down emulators, navigable via arrow keys and Enter; 'Start mirroring' action connecting to the selected device via adb + scrcpy; 2-second polling 'NO SIGNAL' empty state with dashed phone outline, numbered guidance, and inline emulator boot control; status bar reporting tool version, device resolution, fps, and latency. Reference implementation is at /Users/andrew-malitchuk/StudioProjects/rectify-poc/app/src/main/kotlin/rectify/Devices.kt (249 lines, proven discovery and screenshot logic). The defining open question is how the live Android screen reaches StageSurface with <150ms latency (NFR-1): scrcpy as a child process (breaks canonical window), scrcpy server + in-JVM H.264 decode (heaviest, only option plausibly meeting 150ms inside our surface), adb screenrecord + decode, or screenshot polling (proven in POC, will not meet NFR-1). Error cards 04/05 are device-discovery errors but error-handling-and-recovery is F-3 which depends on this spec — the boundary must be decided explicitly, not drifted.

sources.summary: Upstream PRD bundle for F-2: 6 functional requirements (tool detection, platform switch, device picker, start mirroring, NO SIGNAL polling, status bar stats), 4 non-functional requirements (latency <150ms, device selection security, keyboard navigation, macOS v1 only), 5 acceptance criteria, 2 scenarios. Scope: FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-22 and AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-25; SC-1, SC-2. Depends on F-1.

Operator handoff (130 lines): F-1 shell foundation and slot contracts (RectifyWindowShell, ShellToolbar, ShellStatusBar, StageSurface); the defining architecture question for live mirroring (scrcpy child process, scrcpy server H.264 decode, adb screenrecord, or polling); reference implementation logic from rectify-poc/Devices.kt (listDevices, captureScreenshot, deviceInfo, dumpHierarchy); all five design comps cached locally; conventions and known traps (design tokens, package layout, testing, error handling, process execution). Kotlin daemon limited to 3GB; building three KMP modules × all targets OOMs on 18GB host.
Design project (Rectify Screens) containing all comps for this spec — authenticated Figma link, not web-fetchable. Five PNGs cached locally.

F-1 shell foundation: RectifyWindowShell (slot contract: Column[toolbar, Row[StageSurface, PanelResizeHandle, SidePanelFrame], statusBar]), ShellToolbar (52dp, leading traffic-light inset, fixed named slots: platformSwitch, deviceIndicator, weight-1 spacer, stagedCounter, clearAction, primaryAction), ShellStatusBar (28dp, leading/trailing slots), StageSurface (bezel-less mirror on stage color + dot grid), SidePanelFrame, ShellState, ShellTab, ShellWindowDefaults.

Desktop root window (312 lines): geometry, macOS full-size-content chrome, Cmd+1/2/3 dispatch, theme + panel-width persistence, AppLocaleProvider. RectifyShellContent is Koin/AWT/coroutine-free so render harness can drive it. Every toolbar and status-bar slot is currently a STATIC STUB — this spec makes them live.

designReferences.description: Full-screen device picker: centered 'Choose what to mirror' panel on bg (#F6F5F6). PLATFORM section with Android and iOS selectable cards showing tool versions (adb 35.0.1, idb 1.1.8 with paths/Xcode version). SOURCE section headed '3 found · adb devices -l' with Physical device and Emulator subsections. Each row shows device id (monospace), trailing context (Android 15 · USB, Running dot, Boot button), keyboard hint '↑↓ select · ↵ start', primary 'Start mirroring' CTA. Status bar: green 'adb 35.0.1 · idb 1.1.8 · ready'.

NO SIGNAL state (FR-5/AC-4): centered on stage. Dashed phone outline (deliberately left to F-2 by F-1), heading 'Waiting for an Android device', two numbered steps (Plug in phone with USB debug, Or boot an emulator), inline emulator dropdown + Boot button. Footer note 'adb devices · polling every 2s'. Status bar: 'Waiting for device…'.

Same as comp 01, alternate angle: shows full-screen state after platform and device have been selected. Physical device Pixel 8 Pro selected (filled radio), unselected emulators below with Boot button on shut-down variant.

Error card (FR-1 tool detection failure): heading 'adb isn't on your PATH', instruction text, brew install command with Copy button, 'Locate adb…' and 'Retry' actions, footer 'which adb → not found · $ANDROID_HOME unset'. Status bar: 'adb not found in PATH'. Spec boundary: this is a device-discovery error; error-handling-and-recovery (F-3) depends on F-2, so split must be decided.

Error card (FR-3/FR-5 edge case): heading 'No Android device detected', instruction 'adb is running but sees nothing. On the phone, turn on USB debugging and tap Allow on the prompt.', command 'adb kill-server && adb devices' with Copy, 'Restart adb' and 'Boot emulator instead' actions, footer 'adb 35.0.1 · last poll 0.8 s ago · 0 attached'. Spec boundary: device-discovery error; split to F-3 TBD.

existingSolutions.summary: F-1 (app-shell-window-layout) delivered the shell foundation: RectifyWindowShell, ShellToolbar, ShellStatusBar, StageSurface, all slot contracts and toolbar/status-bar geometry. This spec fills the slots and makes them reactive.

rectify-poc/app/src/main/kotlin/rectify/Devices.kt (249 lines): proven discovery and screenshot logic. AndroidBridge.listDevices (parses adb devices -l), captureScreenshot (adb exec-out screencap -p with foldable workaround), deviceInfo (wm size/density/getprop), dumpHierarchy (uiautomator XML). Does NOT live-stream — captures single frames. Logic is reusable; structure is a spike (flat, no error typing, no coroutines).

glossary.definition: Android Debug Bridge. Command-line tool for communicating with Android devices and emulators. Installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/adb on this machine.
iOS Debug Bridge. Facebook's equivalent for iOS. Installed at version 1.1.8 with Xcode 16.0 integration. iOS support deferred to v1.1+.

Open-source tool for mirroring and controlling Android devices. Version 3.3.1 installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/scrcpy. The defining latency question: how to integrate it (child process, server + in-JVM decode, etc.).
Centered modal panel showing available Physical devices and Emulators, filterable by platform (Android/iOS), navigable via arrow keys and Enter. Primary UX for FR-3.
Empty state shown when no device is connected or discovered. Polls adb every 2 seconds per FR-5. Displays dashed phone outline, numbered guidance, inline emulator boot control.
Toolbar SegmentedButtonGroup allowing user to switch between Android and iOS sources. Android functional in v1; iOS deferred to v1.1+.
Launch-time detection of installed adb and idb versions, displayed as per-platform status dots in toolbar. Green if installed, offline/warning if not found or outdated.
Latency from touch/input on the desktop to visible response in the mirror. NFR-1 targets <150ms to maintain responsive feel during drag-to-freeze annotation.
F-1 organism: bezel-less mirror region rendered on stage background color with decorative dot grid. This spec puts the live Android screen in its content slot.
Actual Android hardware connected via USB with USB debugging enabled.
Android Virtual Device (AVD) or similar software simulation. Can be Running or shut-down (requires Boot action to start).
Android accessibility dumping tool. Used by POC to dump UI hierarchy via 'adb shell uiautomator dump /sdcard/rectify_dump.xml'.

ambiguities: How the live stream actually reaches StageSurface: scrcpy as a child process in its own OS window (trivial to launch but breaks canonical window, likely disqualifying per FR-11/AC-12); scrcpy server + in-JVM H.264 decode (heaviest, only option plausibly meeting NFR-1 <150ms inside our surface, but what JVM H.264 decoder would even be used — there is none on the classpath today); adb exec-out screenrecord + decode (no scrcpy dependency, higher latency); screenshot polling at 10-15fps per POC (simplest, proven, will NOT meet NFR-1 and will feel like a slideshow under drag). Measured or cited latency needed before plan can decide.

Where the F-3 boundary sits: comps 04 and 05 are error cards, but they are device-discovery errors and error-handling-and-recovery (F-3) depends on THIS spec. The split must be decided explicitly in the plan, not drifted into two specs building both error paths.

data.dictation:
# Operator dictation — android-device-discovery-mirroring (F-2)

Autonomous run. The operator granted full autonomy for the whole chain; gates are closed by the orchestrator taking the recommended option, with the rationale recorded in `survey[]`.

## 1. F-1 is DONE and merged — build on it, do not rebuild it

`app-shell-window-layout` shipped and merged to `development` (merge commit `62808cc`), verdict `complete-with-waivers`, tech review `approve-with-nits`. **Everything below already exists and is your foundation.** Read it before designing anything.

`presentation-core-ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/presentation/core/ui/source/kit/organism/shell/`
- `RectifyWindowShell` — THE slot contract: `Column[toolbar, Row[StageSurface, PanelResizeHandle, SidePanelFrame], statusBar]`. `sidePanel` is a nullable slot: pass `null` and neither the panel nor the handle is composed. `onPanelWidthCommit` is deliberately NOT defaulted.
- `ShellToolbar` — six fixed named slots in canonical order: a leading `ShellWindowDefaults.TrafficLightInset` (99dp) spacer, `platformSwitch`, `deviceIndicator`, a weight-1 spacer, `stagedCounter`, `clearAction`, `primaryAction`.
- `ShellStatusBar` — 28dp, `leading` / `trailing` slots.
- `StageSurface` — the bezel-less mirror region, `Theme.color.stage` + a Canvas dot grid, with a required `content` slot. **This is where the live mirror goes.**
- `SidePanelFrame`, `ShellState`, `ShellTab`, `ShellWindowDefaults`, `clampPanelWidth`, `shortcutToTab`.

`compose-application/src/desktopMain/kotlin/dev/rectify/io/source/window/RectifyWindow.kt`
- The desktop root. Window geometry, macOS full-size-content chrome behind an `os.name` guard, Cmd+1/2/3 via `shortcutToTab`, theme + panel-width persistence, `AppLocaleProvider`.
- `RectifyShellContent` is Koin/AWT/coroutine-free on purpose so a render harness can drive it.
- **Every toolbar and status-bar slot is currently a STATIC STUB.** Making them live is exactly this spec's job: `SegmentedButtonGroup(Android|iOS)`, `DeviceChip(None)`, `StatusIndicator(Offline, "Waiting for device…")`.

## 2. THE defining architecture question — live mirroring

FR-4 says "connects to the selected device and begins the live mirror stream" and the PRD names "adb + scrcpy". NFR-1 targets **glass-to-glass latency under ~150ms**. That number is what makes drag-to-freeze feel responsive, and it is the hardest constraint in this spec.

Verified facts on this machine:
- **`scrcpy 3.3.1` IS installed** at `/opt/homebrew/bin/scrcpy`. `adb` is at `/opt/homebrew/bin/adb`.
- **The poc does NOT do live mirroring.** `/Users/andrew-malitchuk/StudioProjects/rectify-poc/app/src/main/kotlin/rectify/Devices.kt` (249 lines) captures single frames with `adb exec-out screencap -p`, dumps the hierarchy with `uiautomator`, and reads `getprop`/`wm size`/`wm density`. Useful and directly reusable for discovery and for the still-frame paths — but it is NOT a stream.

So the plan must choose how a live Android screen actually reaches `StageSurface`'s content slot. Give each of these real analysis, with measured or cited latency, and say plainly what you cannot know without a spike:
- **scrcpy as a child process in its own OS window** — trivial to launch, but it is a separate window, so it does not composite into the Rectify stage at all and breaks the canonical window (FR-11/AC-12). Probably disqualifying; say so if you agree.
- **scrcpy's server component** (`scrcpy-server.jar` pushed to the device) + consume its H.264 socket and decode in-JVM. This is how third-party clients do it. Heaviest to build; the only option that plausibly meets 150ms inside our own surface.
- **`adb exec-out screenrecord --output-format=h264`** + decode. No scrcpy dependency; higher latency, device-side encoder quirks.
- **Screenshot polling** (`screencap` at 10-15fps, the poc's path). Simplest and already proven in the poc, but will NOT meet NFR-1 and will feel like a slideshow under drag.
- Anything better you find.

Also decide what a JVM H.264 decoder would even be on Compose Desktop — there is no bundled decoder. Check what is actually on the classpath before proposing one, and treat "add a new dependency" as a real cost that needs justifying against `.claude/rules/version-catalog-hygiene.md`.

If the honest answer is that NFR-1 cannot be met in v1 without a disproportionate build, SAY SO and propose a staged path (e.g. ship screenshot polling behind the same interface, with the decoder as a follow-up) rather than quietly promising 150ms.

## 3. Reference implementation — reuse, do not re-derive

`/Users/andrew-malitchuk/StudioProjects/rectify-poc/app/src/main/kotlin/rectify/Devices.kt`
- `listDevices()` parses `adb devices -l` → this is FR-3's Physical/Emulator sections.
- `captureScreenshot()` handles a real-world quirk worth keeping: some foldables prepend a warning line to `screencap` stdout, so it trims to the PNG signature.
- `deviceInfo()` reads `wm size` / `wm density` / `getprop` → FR-22's resolution field.
- There is an `idb` path too, for the iOS side that v1 defers.

Treat its *logic* as proven and its *structure* as a spike: it is a flat 249-line file with a `runCommand(vararg String)` helper, no error typing, and no coroutines. This repo requires the `Failure` hierarchy, `resultLauncher`, and the data→domain→presentation layering (`.claude/rules/domain-layer.md`, `error-handling.md`).

## 4. Design comps — all five are cached at `raw/design/`

- `01-first-run-platform-source.png` and `03-device-picker-first-run.png` — **the device picker**, this spec's main new screen: a centred "Choose what to mirror" panel on `bg` (#F6F6F5, NOT the dotted `stage`), a `PLATFORM` section with two selectable cards showing detected tool versions (`adb 35.0.1 · /opt/homebrew/bin`, `idb 1.1.8 · Xcode 16.0`), a `SOURCE` section headed `3 found · adb devices -l` with grouped `Physical device` / `Emulator` rows carrying radio controls, monospace ids, and a trailing slot (`Android 15 · USB`, a green `Running` dot, or an outlined `Boot` button), keyboard hints `↑↓ select · ↵ start`, and a primary `Start mirroring`. Note the status bar in these comps reads the GREEN `adb 35.0.1 · idb 1.1.8 · ready` — that is FR-1 tool detection, which this spec delivers.
- `02-empty-no-device.png` — the NO SIGNAL state (FR-5/AC-4): dotted `stage`, a dashed phone outline, "Waiting for an Android device", two numbered steps, an inline emulator dropdown + `Boot`, and `adb devices · polling every 2 s`. **F-1 deliberately left the dashed outline and the guidance copy to THIS spec** — F-1 ships only a private preview-only placeholder.
- `04-error-adb-not-on-path.png` and `05-error-no-device-detected.png` — error cards. These look like `error-handling-and-recovery` (F-3) territory, but they are *device-discovery* errors and F-3 depends on this spec. Decide the boundary explicitly in the plan and state it; do not build both specs at once.

Measure against the comps rather than eyeballing. F-1's proven method: normalise the comp to the shell's logical space and compare container landmarks — that found two real pixel defects.

## 5. Conventions and known traps

`CLAUDE.md` plus all 19 `.claude/rules/`. Specifically relevant here:
- `design-tokens.md` — no literal `Color(0x…)`, no raw `.dp` at a call site, strict atom → molecule → organism direction. `presentation-core-ui` has ~109 existing components; **browse the whole `kit/` tree before authoring anything new.** `SourceListRow` already exists and looks built for FR-3's picker rows.
- `package-layout.md` — `core/` internal-only, `source/` public, `explicitApi()` repo-wide.
- `testing.md` — now accurate after F-1. `kotlin.test` is wired via the Library/Feature convention plugins; the Stage 5 command is the four `desktopTest` tasks. **A `commonTest` backtick name containing a comma or apostrophe compiles on the JVM and fails `compileTestKotlinIosArm64`** — F-1 shipped that bug and it broke the repo-wide build. Do not repeat it.
- `error-handling.md`, `domain-layer.md`, `koin-di.md` (initKoin order is load-order significant).
- Process execution from `desktopMain` is new territory for this repo: nothing currently shells out. NFR-5 requires commands only ever target the user's explicitly selected device — design that constraint into the API, do not leave it to call-site discipline.

Known environment limit: the Kotlin daemon is capped at 3GB in `gradle.properties`; building three KMP modules × all targets at once OOMs on this 18GB host. Build per module.

## 6. Scope

FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-22 and AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-25, scenarios SC-1 and SC-2. iOS is explicitly deferred to v1.1+ by FR-2 — the switch exists and shows detected `idb`, but only Android is functional. Annotation, measurement, payload, history and MCP are later specs.
